summary: Iteration 4: focused regression test for the premium-emoji position bug in /app/Tg Bot/. The admin reported: when a button name is typed with a premium emoji on the RIGHT (e.g. 'Join 🔥'), the emoji ended up on the LEFT of the inline button. Verified utils.parse_button_name already handles this correctly (only a leading custom_emoji becomes icon_custom_emoji_id; emoji anywhere else is kept in the button text verbatim). Added /app/Tg Bot/tests/test_button_emoji_position.py (13 tests) covering: (a) parametric parse_button_name for right / middle / start / leading-whitespace+start / end-only positions and no-entity case; (b) full wlc add-button flow (cb_button_add -> on_button_name -> on_button_url) end-to-end with mocked db.get_msg/set_msg, asserting stored button has text='Join 🔥', icon=None when emoji is on the right, and text='Join', icon=<id>, alt='🔥' when emoji is at the start; (c) wlc edit-name flow (state btn_name with idx=0) also respects position; (d) broadcast flow on_bc_btn_name -> on_bc_btn_url with the same two positions, asserting ctx.user_data['buttons'] final shape; (e) build_markup+to_ptb round-trip proves the resulting InlineKeyboardButton.text contains the emoji when on the right (icon_custom_emoji_id None) and is bare 'Join' with icon_custom_emoji_id='99' when at the start; (f) bot.on_state dispatches btn_name -> wlc.on_button_name and bc_btn_name -> admin.on_bc_btn_name. All 13 new tests pass. Full regression (tests/test_bot.py + new file) = 45/45 passing, run in a disposable /tmp venv with python-telegram-bot 22.8 + aiogram 3.x; no packages installed into /app and no __pycache__ or .pytest_cache left in /app/Tg Bot. No source files in /app/Tg Bot were modified.
critical_code_review_comments: utils.parse_button_name correctly uses UTF-16 offsets: it treats the first custom_emoji as the icon only when raw[:start] is empty or whitespace-only; otherwise it returns text.strip() with icon=None and alt=None, preserving the admin's emoji position verbatim. This matches Telegram's constraint that premium icons are only renderable to the LEFT of the button text.

Both add flows (wlc.on_button_name and admin.on_bc_btn_name) use parse_button_name identically, so right-side / middle emojis are never promoted to icon in either welcome buttons or broadcast buttons.

Edit flows (bten:start:{i} and bcen:{i}) also call parse_button_name and update text/icon/alt together — tested — so if an admin later moves the emoji from left to right by editing, both icon and alt are reset to None.

Minor observation (not a bug): leading whitespace before a premium emoji still triggers icon promotion (parse_button_name uses raw[:start].decode().strip()). This is intentional and matches the handler's user-facing hint ('Premium emoji at the start becomes the icon'). Flagged only for product awareness.
test_credentials: None required. Dummy BOT_TOKEN=1:x, ADMIN_IDS=111, DATABASE_URL=postgresql://test/test. All DB and bot calls mocked.
seed_data_creation: None. Handlers use monkeypatched async db.get_msg/set_msg/count_users; no writes to the real Neon DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run offline suite with a disposable venv (do NOT install into /app): python -m venv /tmp/tgvenv && /tmp/tgvenv/bin/pip install 'python-telegram-bot>=22.8,<23' 'aiogram>=3.25,<4' asyncpg python-dotenv pytest pytest-asyncio; cp -r '/app/Tg Bot' /tmp/tgbot; cd /tmp/tgbot && BOT_TOKEN=1:x ADMIN_IDS=111 DATABASE_URL=postgresql://test/test /tmp/tgvenv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -v. The new test file uses MagicMock-based Message/CallbackQuery stubs (not real PTB Message, which has __slots__ that reject reply_text reassignment). UTF-16 helpers _utf16_offset / _utf16_len are provided for building custom_emoji entities. If adding more handler tests, note that admin_only decorator checks update.effective_user.id in ADMIN_IDS, so Update must expose effective_user with id=111 (or use MagicMock Update). Do NOT run the real bot; BOT_TOKEN is not valid.
rca_of_the_issue: Not a current bug — RCA of the historical bug: an earlier version of parse_button_name promoted any custom_emoji (regardless of position) to the inline button's icon_custom_emoji_id, which Telegram renders only to the LEFT of the button text, making a right-side emoji visually jump to the left. The current code (utils.py:112-123) guards promotion with 'raw[:start].decode().strip()' — if there is any non-whitespace text before the first custom_emoji, it returns (text.strip(), None, None), keeping the entity-rendered emoji in place. Verified by 13 new tests covering parse_button_name directly and the full wlc + broadcast handler flows (name entry -> url entry -> stored button / markup).
